title: Chicago: no street funerals, blowing taps
summary: In Chicago Miller played the street only for the Elks convention and blew taps for burials, with Kelly and Jimmy Wade.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Chicago? Well, they didn't do that there until they started getting all in and banged down there. The only thing I would play there on the streets was for the Elks' big convention. But I never played a funeral. And when people died there, I went and blew taps twice. I built a guy, Kelly, and another boy named Jimmy Wade. I didn't have a bang.
Just blew taps. Jimmy Wade the trumpet.
Yeah. My wife, I didn't bang all the time.
I made those records, but they did good, too.
Yeah, Jimmy Lee was a nice little fella.
